headline: Medium prompt-injection and data-leakage risks arise from shared file-based workflows; Copilot’s closed-source docs-only profile and unstructured’s document parsing can amplify downstream errors.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Copilot reads repo context and open editor buffers, while unstructured reads documents and text; if unstructured output is copied into Copilot inputs, attacker-controlled document content can steer prompts. This is not provably blocked by either profile, and the shared file-based bridge is plausible in default workflows.
conditions: IF unstructured output is pasted or saved into files that Copilot reads as repo context or open buffers, injection is possible.
IF document content contains adversarial instructions and Copilot treats file content as trusted, prompt steering can occur.
mitigations: Keep unstructured outputs in a separate folder not opened in Copilot.
Add a manual review step before copying parsed text into prompts.
Strip instructions/markup from parsed documents before reuse.
Use read-only exports for document parsing outputs.
requires-engineering: add provenance labels to parsed text before any LLM consumption.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Copilot touches source code and open buffers and sends requests to api.githubcopilot.com; unstructured processes documents, images, and text with allowlisted egress. If the same workspace contains sensitive documents or code, both agents can expose overlapping data classes through their respective network paths.
conditions: IF sensitive documents are placed in the same workspace as code, both agents can access them.
IF unstructured sends parsed document content to allowlisted external services, leakage can extend beyond the local workspace.
mitigations: Separate code and document workspaces.
Remove sensitive files before running either agent.
Restrict unstructured to non-sensitive documents only.
Review outbound allowlists for document-processing jobs.
requires-engineering: enforce per-folder access controls and DLP scanning.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents can write the filesystem, and Copilot can modify git state while unstructured can spawn subprocesses and install packages. In a shared directory, concurrent edits or generated artifacts can overwrite each other even though Copilot’s editor-scoped isolation reduces some risk.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same directory, file overwrite conflicts can occur.
IF unstructured generates artifacts while Copilot edits the repo, git state divergence can happen.
mitigations: Run each agent in a separate working tree.
Pause one agent while the other writes files.
Commit or stash changes before switching agents.
Keep generated documents outside the git repo.
requires-engineering: add locking around shared mutable paths.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Copilot can propose edits for human review, and unstructured can transform documents into text that may be treated as authoritative input. If downstream users or automation trust unstructured output and then accept Copilot’s edits without verification, errors can cascade across both agents.
conditions: IF parsed document text is used as source-of-truth for Copilot prompts, hallucinated or malformed extraction can propagate.
IF Copilot edits are accepted without human review, downstream mistakes can be committed.
mitigations: Verify extracted facts against the original document.
Require human review before accepting Copilot edits.
Use schema validation on unstructured outputs.
Limit Copilot to refactoring tasks on verified inputs.
requires-engineering: add automated cross-checks between source documents and extracted fields.

E_compliance.rationale: Copilot is closed-source and vendor-hosted with GitHub repo OAuth context, while unstructured is open-source and containerized with allowlisted egress. The profiles do not show a direct residency or certification mismatch, but mixed handling of code and documents can create compliance gaps if sensitive data is co-located.
conditions: IF regulated documents are stored alongside code in the same workspace, policy separation may be violated.
IF organizational policy requires local-only processing, Copilot’s vendor API use conflicts with it.
mitigations: Keep regulated documents out of Copilot workspaces.
Use unstructured only in approved containers.
Review data-handling policies for GitHub-hosted AI services.
Document which data classes each agent may process.
requires-engineering: implement policy-based routing by data classification.
